pr_title: Do not reorder HTTP header values
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
fix #63833 & #63831
Author: feiyun0112
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`
Milestone: -

This will now additionally allocate a `List<HeaderStoreItemInfoValue>`, `HeaderStoreItemInfoValue[]` and `HeaderStoreItemInfoValue` even if only a single valid value was added.

I think we should keep the field as `object` and allocate the `List<object>` on demand if more than 1 value is added.

We can also avoid allocating the `HeaderStoreItemInfoValue` for each parsed value. Instead, we can store the values as `object`s like before, but use a new `internal record InvalidValue(string Value)` to differentiate between parsed/invalid values. I.e. only paying the extra cost for invalid values.

I also don't believe this will solve #63831 as that deals with the enumeration order when values are both parsed and unparsed.

@stephentoub @geoffkizer please take a look at this in case I'm missing something major here.

The general gist of changes is:
- Instead of keeping `Raw`, `Invalid`, `Parsed` fields on the `HeaderStoreItemInfo`, we now have `Raw`, `ParsedAndInvalid`
  - Except for `Cache-Control`, valid/invalid values can be added in any order and that will be preserved during enumeration
  - `Cache-Control` is special in that it merges parsed values into a single `parsed` entry, and we lose ordering if valid/invalid values are interleaved
- Invalid values are differentiated from parsed objects in the same list by being stored in a `record InvalidValue(string Value)`, and we then use type checks when searching through the list
- All the logic around handling parsed/invalid is updated to account for the above

No perf tests were run around this yet, but the expected differences should be rather negligible:
- No effect on `NonValidated` headers
- For parsed values, the `HeaderStoreItemInfo` is smaller by 1 reference (fewer bytes, less work for the GC)
- Some operations with parsed values become more expensive due to additional type checks
- Invalid values allocate an extra `InvalidValue` object when parsed (class with 1 reference field)
I don't think this fixes #63831, does it? At least, I didn't see where, and I didn't see a test case for it. Did I miss it?

> I don't think this fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/63831, does it?

It does not. I removed it from the PR description to avoid confusion.
@feiyun0112 It appears [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/65249#discussion_r828359536) has been marked as resolved multiple times - is there an associated change I missed?

issue_context.title: Handling of "invalid" HTTP header values results in values being incorrectly reordered
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
When we parse known multi-valued headers like Accept, we store any "invalid" values (i.e. values we couldn't parse) separately so that they will still be written to the wire and can still be enumerated via NonValidated. However, these invalid values are reordered relative to the rest of the values so that they always appear after valid values. Repro code: ```csharp HttpRequestMessage request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "http://microsoft.com"); request.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Accept", "text/bar"); request.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Accept", "invalid"); request.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Accept", "text/baz"); Console.WriteLine("NonValidated before parsing (correct):"); PrintHeadersNonValidated(request); // Force parsing _ = request.Headers.Accept.Count; Console.WriteLine("NonValidated after parsing (incorrect):"); PrintHeadersNonValidated(request); static void PrintHeadersNonValidated(HttpRequestMessage request) { foreach (var header in request.Headers.NonValidated) { Console.WriteLine($" {header.Key}:"); foreach (var value in header.Value) { Console.WriteLine($" {value}"); } } Console.WriteLine(); } ``` Output: ``` NonValidated before parsing (correct): Accept: text/bar invalid text/baz NonValidated after parsing (incorrect): Accept: text/bar text/baz invalid ``` Note that this behavior is not limited to NonValidated -- it affects how the request headers are written to the wire when the request is sent.
Author: geoffkizer
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

Instead of duplicating the values in both fields, consider adding a new object
`internal record InvalidValue(string Value)` to represent invalid values inside `ParsedAndInvalidValues`.

`IsInvalidValue(object value)` then becomes `values is InvalidValue` instead of searching the whole list.
